question: What is the maximum time you should spend on a single suction pass for an adult patient?

options.A: One full minute
options.B: Two to three minutes
options.C: 10 to 15 seconds
options.D: 30 to 45 seconds

explanation: Always keep an eye on your watch! Suctioning takes away oxygen, so limit it to 10-15 seconds max to keep your patient safe from low oxygen levels.

question: Why does rapid international travel pose a major risk during an outbreak?

options.A: It allows a local pathogen to spread globally in hours
options.B: It prevents local clinics from ordering basic supplies
options.C: It automatically destroys the genetic code of medications
options.D: It forces travelers to abandon all personal hygiene habits

explanation: Fast global movement means an infected person can board a plane while healthy and land in another country before showing symptoms. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h2)

question: What is the recommended minimum time for brushing teeth properly?

options.A: Two full minutes
options.B: Five exact minutes
options.C: Thirty total seconds
options.D: Ten brief seconds

explanation: Brushing for at least two minutes gives you enough time to reach all tooth surfaces and get rid of stubborn plaque.

question: What does an 'out-of-pocket' payment system mean for a patient?

options.A: Patients pay directly for medical services themselves
options.B: The government covers all medical bills automatically
options.C: Health insurance pays every cent of hospital costs
options.D: Services are provided entirely free of charge

explanation: Spot on! Out-of-pocket means the patient pays cash right there at the point of care out of their own wallet.

question: What is an appropriate immediate nursing intervention for a newborn diagnosed with a skull injury?

options.A: Place the infant flat without any head support
options.B: Minimize handling to prevent further trauma
options.C: Encourage vigorous crying to expand the lungs
options.D: Perform daily head massage to reduce swelling

explanation: Reducing unnecessary handling and stimulation helps protect the injured skull and prevents spikes in intracranial pressure. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h5)

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation?

options.A: Monitoring focuses on budget spending, while evaluation focuses only on nursing salaries
options.B: Monitoring is done by the community, while evaluation is done strictly by the government
options.C: Monitoring tracks activities during implementation, while evaluation measures final outcomes and impact
options.D: Monitoring happens after the project ends, while evaluation happens before it starts

explanation: Think of monitoring as checking your progress *while* running the race, and evaluation as looking at the results *after* you cross the finish line.

question: What is the medical term for difficulty swallowing?

options.A: Deglutition
options.B: Aspiration
options.C: Dysphagia
options.D: Peristalsis

explanation: Dysphagia is the clinical term used when a patient experiences trouble moving food or liquid from the mouth to the stomach safely. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h1)

question: What is an important job for nurse managers who deal with financial data?

options.A: Approving pharmaceutical manufacturing licenses
options.B: Fixing broken hospital electrical wiring
options.C: Defending staffing levels and resource needs
options.D: Auditing national tax collection records

explanation: Having good cost data lets nurse managers confidently fight for enough staff and supplies to keep patients safe.

question: How should an emotionally intelligent leader respond to a nurse dealing with burnout?

options.A: By validating their feelings and offering meaningful support
options.B: By giving them a formal warning for poor productivity
options.C: By ignoring the issue so it resolves itself over time
options.D: By assigning them extra weekend shifts to build toughness

explanation: Burnout is real. A great leader spots the exhaustion, listens with empathy, and offers genuine support instead of piling on more stress or punishment.

question: What happens when you cram way too much data into a single research table?

options.A: It changes the fundamental type of the study
options.B: Journals will charge extra money for the paper weight
options.C: It becomes confusing and hard for readers to digest
options.D: It automatically makes all the calculations mathematically incorrect

explanation: Tables are supposed to simplify life, not overwhelm the brain. Too much data in one spot defeats the whole purpose!

question: Why might a doctor order a biopsy for a vulval lump in an older adult patient?

options.A: To measure the exact amount of fluid inside the cyst
options.B: To check and make sure the persistent or unusual mass is not cancerous
options.C: To prove that the cyst started from an infected hair follicle
options.D: To help the fluid sac absorb faster on its own

explanation: Any unusual or stubborn lump in older women needs a quick tissue check (biopsy) just to be 100% sure it isn't malignant.

question: What is the best mindset for a nurse handling conflict within the healthcare team?

options.A: Viewing conflict as a problem to solve together
options.B: Reporting every minor disagreement to the police
options.C: Ignoring the argument until someone else fixes it
options.D: Proving that the other person is completely wrong

explanation: You got it! Tackling disagreements as a team issue rather than a personal fight helps everyone reach a peaceful, patient-centered solution.

question: Why are school-aged children especially prone to getting heavy worm infections?

options.A: Children have an increased biological requirement for adult worms
options.B: Stomach acid levels in children are too high for parasites to tolerate
options.C: Frequent outdoor play and hand-to-mouth behaviors increase exposure
options.D: Their immune systems permanently block all antihelminthic treatments

explanation: Kids love to play outside in the dirt, and with habits like putting unwashed hands in their mouths, they easily pick up parasite eggs.

question: A community health nurse notices high rates of childhood stunting and anemia in an isolated village. What underlying distribution problem is most likely contributing to this?

options.A: An oversupply of refrigerated trucks delivering too many vegetables
options.B: Excessive availability of free nutritional supplements from clinics
options.C: Strict local laws that prohibit families from cooking traditional meals
options.D: Inability to consistently transport diverse, fresh foods to the area

explanation: Poor transport links starve remote populations of the varied nutrients required for healthy childhood development. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h7)

question: What is the main goal of giving Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) to someone with HIV?

options.A: To replace damaged CD4 cells with donor bone marrow
options.B: To suppress viral replication to undetectable levels
options.C: To cure opportunistic infections without antibiotics
options.D: To completely eradicate the virus from every body cell

explanation: ART stops the virus from multiplying, keeping viral counts super low and protecting the immune system.

question: In the popular OLDCARTS pain assessment mnemonic, what does the letter 'L' stand for?

options.A: Limit
options.B: Location
options.C: Length
options.D: Level

explanation: Correct! 'L' stands for location. It helps you pinpoint exactly where on the body the patient is hurting.

question: When giving nursing care after an abortion, what does a holistic approach mainly mean?

options.A: Recognizing overlapping systemic illnesses
options.B: Treating only physical symptoms
options.C: Focusing solely on uterine health
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately

explanation: Great nursing looks at the whole person! Comprehensive care means looking beyond just the reproductive system to see how other health conditions might affect the patient's recovery.

question: A student smells fresh jollof rice and instantly feels hungry and happy. Which brain area drives this?

options.A: Primary visual and motor cortices
options.B: Cerebellum and spinal reflex arcs
options.C: Somatosensory parietal association areas
options.D: Limbic system and hypothalamus

explanation: Exactly! Connections to our limbic system and hypothalamus turn simple scent molecules into warm feelings of hunger, comfort, and happy memories.

question: In the popular SOAP charting format, what does the letter 'O' stand for?

options.A: Optimal outcome
options.B: Objective data
options.C: Ongoing order
options.D: Observed opinion

explanation: You've got this! 'O' is for objective data—the things you can actually measure and see, like vital signs and physical exam results.

question: Why does the human body need food nutrients?

options.A: To completely prevent all known infectious diseases
options.B: To speed up the physical digestion of solid wastes
options.C: To increase the total volume of blood in circulation
options.D: To provide substances needed for energy, growth, and repair

explanation: Think of nutrients as the fuel and building blocks your body uses every single day to stay active, grow, and heal wounds. You've got this!

question: On day four after delivery, a breastfeeding mother tells you she feels overwhelmed and cries easily when the baby fusses, but she loves holding her baby and sleeps well when the baby sleeps. What is your best response?

options.A: Inform her that she shows classic signs of postpartum psychosis
options.B: Tell her to stop breastfeeding immediately to stabilize her hormones
options.C: Reassure her that these feelings are common postpartum blues and will likely pass soon
options.D: Immediately arrange an emergency psychiatric admission for depression

explanation: Tearfulness and mood swings in the first two weeks are totally normal 'baby blues.' A listening ear and gentle reassurance work wonders here!

question: A patient asks if changing their diet and exercising can help with mild erectile dysfunction. What is the best response?

options.A: Once sexual dysfunction starts, lifestyle changes can never reverse it
options.B: Diet and exercise only affect heart disease and have no link to sexual function
options.C: You should stop exercising immediately to preserve your energy
options.D: Lifestyle changes improve blood circulation and can significantly benefit sexual health

explanation: Absolutely! What is good for the heart is good for sexual health. Better circulation means better physical function overall.

question: What protective gear is a must-have when preparing cytotoxic drugs?

options.A: Surgical masks without eye shields
options.B: Regular sterile procedural gloves
options.C: Standard latex gloves and cloth lab coats
options.D: Chemotherapy-tested gloves and gowns

explanation: Safety first! Regular gloves are too thin for these strong drugs, so nurses wear special chemo-rated gear to stay safe.

question: Why is recovery in rehabilitation often described as non-linear or up-and-down?

options.A: Therapists change goals randomly every single day
options.B: Insurance companies dictate how many phases a patient must skip
options.C: Medical staff rarely document patient improvements
options.D: Patients often experience setbacks that require adjusting the care plan

explanation: Healing isn't a straight line! Good days and bad days happen, and nurses adjust care plans to match how the patient is feeling.

question: What is the specific, go-to antidote for a paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose?

options.A: Naloxone
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Flumazenil
options.D: Acetylcysteine

explanation: You'll see this often in the ward! Acetylcysteine saves the liver by restocking its natural protector (glutathione) just in time before paracetamol metabolites cause damage.

question: What did the old FDA pregnancy Category X label mean for a medication?

options.A: No animal testing had been performed on the substance
options.B: Human studies proved the drug cured congenital infections
options.C: Fetal risks clearly outweighed any potential therapeutic benefit
options.D: The drug was completely safe for use at any gestational age

explanation: Category X meant 'Do not use!' The danger to the baby was proven and far outweighed any help the drug could give the mother.

question: Why do hospitals prefer phased construction plans over shutting down completely during expansions?

options.A: They allow construction workers to finish the project in one day
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for architectural blueprints
options.C: They prevent the hospital from ever needing future maintenance
options.D: They minimize disruption to ongoing patient care services

explanation: Building section by section allows the hospital to keep its doors open, caring for patients safely while construction happens away from active wards.

question: Apart from direct bedside nursing, what is another key role nurses play in tackling health barriers?

options.A: Passing national laws to regulate international drug importation
options.B: Advocating for health policy reforms and community education
options.C: Setting macroeconomic exchange rates for medical supplies
options.D: Financing the construction of federal tertiary hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Nurses use their frontline experiences to teach communities and push for system changes that make care more accessible.

question: A nurse needs to weigh a patient wearing a heavy leg cast that cannot be taken off. How should this be documented?

options.A: Guess how much the cast weighs and subtract that amount from the scale reading
options.B: Record the weight and add a clear note stating the patient was wearing a leg cast
options.C: Omit the weight entry entirely from the patient chart until the cast comes off
options.D: Record the weight without any mention of the cast so the chart looks normal

explanation: Always document the facts! Adding a note about the cast helps other nurses understand why the weight is higher without guessing.

question: Why does the herbal supplement St. John's wort often cause prescription drugs to fail?

options.A: It coats the stomach lining and stops all oral tablets from dissolving
options.B: It mimics the chemical structure of insulin and lowers blood sugar
options.C: It induces liver enzymes, causing other drugs to break down too fast
options.D: It binds tightly to vitamin K in the gut and prevents blood clotting

explanation: St. John's wort puts the liver into overdrive! It makes the liver clear out other companion medicines so fast that they leave the body before they even have a chance to work.

question: What is the medical term used when a patient's bad reaction stops after the suspected drug is withdrawn?

options.A: Tolerance
options.B: Anaphylaxis
options.C: Dechallenge
options.D: Rechallenge

explanation: Think of 'dechallenge' as un-challenging the body—stopping the medicine to see if the symptoms get better or go away.

question: In a research table, what do we call the leftmost column that lists the main categories?

options.A: Title
options.B: Stub
options.C: Boxhead
options.D: Footnote

explanation: Think of the 'stub' as the leftmost column that holds your row labels or main items being measured, like the names of different vital signs.

question: A postpartum patient who delivered 24 hours ago asks why her blood sugar levels have suddenly dropped back to normal after needing insulin during pregnancy. What is the nurse's best response?

options.A: It is a sign that your kidneys are working too hard to filter extra sugar out of your blood.
options.B: The hormones from the placenta that caused insulin resistance were delivered with the baby.
options.C: This drop is only temporary and your blood sugar will spike again once your milk comes in.
options.D: Your pancreas has suddenly regenerated new cells to process all the sugar in your diet.

explanation: Once the placenta is expelled, the hormones causing gestational insulin resistance vanish, leading to an immediate drop in insulin requirements. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h6)

question: What is the most crucial safety step before placing a hot water bottle on your patient?

options.A: Checking the patient's current blood glucose level
options.B: Testing the temperature of the water and checking the skin
options.C: Asking the patient to sign a formal surgical consent form
options.D: Giving the patient a heavy sleeping pill

explanation: Safety first! Always test the water temperature yourself and check the skin condition to prevent accidental burns.

question: At which spinal level is an intrathecal injection usually performed in adults to avoid damaging the spinal cord?

options.A: C1-C2 or C2-C3
options.B: L3-L4 or L4-L5
options.C: T1-T2 or T2-T3
options.D: S1-S2 or S2-S3

explanation: In adults, the spinal cord ends around the L1-L2 vertebra, so punctures are done lower down at lumbar levels to keep the cord safe. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h2)

question: What is the main danger if the uterine lining is exposed to constant estrogen without enough progesterone to trigger shedding?

options.A: Rapid thinning and complete wasting of the muscle layer
options.B: Sudden development of ovarian cysts on both sides
options.C: Increased risk of endometrial hyperplasia and cancer
options.D: Permanent closure of the cervix

explanation: Without regular periods to clear it out, the uterine lining can overgrow (hyperplasia) from too much unopposed estrogen, which increases cancer risks over time.

question: What is the very first action a nurse should take when suspecting an IV site has infiltrated?

options.A: Stop the infusion and remove the catheter immediately.
options.B: Flush the catheter with sterile saline to clear any local blockage.
options.C: Apply a hot compress directly over the swollen site while the line runs.
options.D: Slow the infusion rate down by half and monitor for one hour.

explanation: Stopping the infusion prevents any more fluid from entering the damaged tissue space, protecting the patient from further injury. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h7)

question: Which of these is a strict, mandatory rule when offering HCT to a client?

options.A: Financial clearance before testing can begin
options.B: Automatic police notification for reactive cases
options.C: Mandatory public announcement of positive results
options.D: Voluntary informed consent from the client

explanation: Great job! A client must always willingly agree to take the test after understanding what it involves, with zero force or pressure.

question: How is a public corporation different from a standard government ministry?

options.A: It is completely privately owned by foreign investors
options.B: It only provides care to international travelers
options.C: It has more financial autonomy and generates revenue
options.D: It does not have to follow any government regulations

explanation: Think of public corporations as businesses set up by the government. Unlike normal ministries that only use tax money, they are designed to bring in their own income!

question: Why is early identification and screening vital in psychiatric nursing?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will never experience stress again
options.B: It prevents mild symptoms from progressing into severe disorders
options.C: It replaces the need for physical health examinations
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any prescription medications

explanation: Early screening identifies issues while they are still manageable, reducing the likelihood of severe impairment or crisis. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h6)

question: Why is it important for nurses to know about local food taboos when caring for patients?

options.A: To determine the financial income of households in the village
options.B: To help identify hidden causes of malnutrition and poor health
options.C: To replace traditional beliefs with foreign culinary recipes
options.D: To enforce strict government fines against cultural practices

explanation: When people avoid certain foods because of taboos, they might miss out on vital nutrients. Spotting this helps you figure out the real reason behind nutritional deficiencies!

question: What is the main job of the rehab nurse within the healthcare team?

options.A: Prescribing physical therapy exercises and ordering diagnostic imaging tests
options.B: Reinforcing therapy skills and coordinating daily care around the clock
options.C: Providing formal legal counseling for insurance claims
options.D: Performing major orthopedic surgeries to correct bone deformities

explanation: Nurses are with the patient 24/7. We tie all the therapies together and keep the healing going round the clock. You are the heartbeat of the ward!

question: Which virus is directly linked to causing Kaposi sarcoma?

options.A: Human papillomavirus
options.B: Epstein-Barr virus
options.C: Human herpesvirus 8
options.D: Cytomegalovirus

explanation: Kaposi sarcoma develops due to a coinfection with human herpesvirus 8 when the immune system is too weak to fight it off.

question: What is the main difference between good (appropriate) polypharmacy and bad (problematic) polypharmacy?

options.A: Problematic polypharmacy only occurs in hospital intensive care units.
options.B: Problematic polypharmacy means the patient refuses to swallow pills.
options.C: Appropriate polypharmacy has clear clinical benefits that outweigh risks.
options.D: Appropriate polypharmacy involves only traditional herbal mixtures.

explanation: Taking many drugs isn't always bad if every single pill has a clear job that helps the patient more than it harms them. That's appropriate polypharmacy!

question: Which of these is NOT a part of Evidence-Based Practice?

options.A: Respecting the unique values and choices of patients
options.B: Following strict historical traditions without question
options.C: Using clinical expertise to guide nursing actions
options.D: Critically appraising current research studies

explanation: Spot on! Evidence-based practice encourages us to question 'we've always done it this way' and instead rely on solid science and critical thinking.

question: How do descriptive statistics help nurses in everyday evidence-based practice?

options.A: By replacing the need for direct physical assessment of patients
options.B: By helping nurses evaluate research reports and quality improvement data
options.C: By allowing nurses to prescribe medications without a physician's order
options.D: By diagnosing complex rare diseases automatically

explanation: Keep it up! Nurses use descriptive stats to read clinical research and understand hospital quality reports so we can give better care to our patients.

question: Why is it ineffective to impose health programs on a community without their input?

options.A: The community will likely ignore or abandon the program because it does not match their real needs
options.B: It violates international aviation laws regarding medical supplies
options.C: It requires too many computers for local health workers
options.D: Local government chairmen are legally forbidden to assist

explanation: If people do not feel ownership or see the relevance of a health initiative, they will not sustain it once outside support stops. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why do many community farming systems encourage seed saving?

options.A: To ensure that all seeds are patented by international corporations
options.B: To preserve climate-resilient seed varieties instead of buying commercial hybrids
options.C: To increase the overall cost of planting basic vegetables
options.D: To prevent any crops from growing during the dry season

explanation: You got it! Saving seeds helps farmers keep traditional, hardy crops growing locally without always having to buy expensive commercial seeds.

question: What is the main goal of having a multi-sectoral referral network for GBV survivors?

options.A: To provide comprehensive medical, legal, and social support through coordinated agencies
options.B: To reduce the total number of follow-up medical visits required
options.C: To transfer all administrative responsibilities away from the hospital
options.D: To ensure the police handle every aspect of the patient's recovery

explanation: Healing takes a village! Teamwork between health workers, legal aid, and social services gives survivors the best all-round support.

question: How does preventing pressure ulcers (bedsores) help a ward save money?

options.A: It eliminates the requirement to purchase any basic patient hygiene supplies.
options.B: It reduces the need for extended hospital stays and expensive specialized treatments.
options.C: It automatically increases the monthly base salary of all attending nurses.
options.D: It allows the hospital to stop tracking patient care hours altogether.

explanation: Good nursing care prevents complications. Stopping bedsores before they start saves patients from pain and saves the hospital from costly, long-term treatments.

question: What is the difference between monitoring and evaluation?

options.A: Monitoring is done by the government, while evaluation is done by children
options.B: Monitoring costs money, while evaluation is completely free
options.C: Monitoring happens continuously during the project, while evaluation measures final results
options.D: Monitoring focuses on drugs, while evaluation focuses on buildings

explanation: Monitoring tracks progress day-by-day, whereas evaluation looks back at the end to see if the main goals were met. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h7)

question: Which group is usually responsible for creating broad health policies and legal frameworks?

options.A: Youth-led organizations
options.B: Government ministries
options.C: Traditional birth attendants
options.D: Private pharmaceutical companies

explanation: That's right! State and federal health ministries carry the official duty of making health policies and legal structures.

question: What is the final outcome of spermatogenesis in human males?

options.A: One large ovum and three polar bodies
options.B: Two identical diploid zygotes
options.C: Four functional spermatozoa
options.D: One functional sperm and three polar bodies

explanation: Great job! Unlike egg formation which makes just one large egg, spermatogenesis neatly divides to produce four healthy, ready-to-go sperm cells.

question: How does tubular secretion differ fundamentally from tubular reabsorption?

options.A: Secretion eliminates useful nutrients, while reabsorption removes metabolic poisons
options.B: Secretion occurs only in the renal cortex, while reabsorption occurs only in the medulla
options.C: Secretion moves substances from blood into the tubule, while reabsorption moves them back to the blood
options.D: Secretion uses passive transport only, while reabsorption requires high blood pressure

explanation: Secretion adds materials to the forming urine from the capillaries, whereas reabsorption rescues valuable substances from the filtrate. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h6)

question: How does keeping a community clean and sanitary help stop the spread of disease using the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: It alters the environment to prevent agent-host contact
options.B: It permanently alters the immune system of the host
options.C: It transforms a viral agent into a harmless bacterium
options.D: It directly destroys the genetic material of the agent

explanation: Great thinking! Good sanitation changes the environment so germs have a much harder time traveling from their source to a human host.

question: What is the biggest advantage of using local community radio stations for NCD health campaigns?

options.A: They replace the need for physical clinical screening examinations
options.B: They can broadcast messages in indigenous languages to reach remote areas
options.C: They are exclusively funded by international public health organizations
options.D: They guarantee that every listener will immediately adopt a healthy diet

explanation: Spot on! Radio bridges the gap, bringing vital health messages right into homes and farms using the local dialects people speak every day.

question: After pricking a finger for blood sugar, why should you wipe away the very first drop?

options.A: It contains tissue fluid that can dilute the sample
options.B: The glucometer machine will reject the first drop
options.C: It prevents the puncture site from bruising
options.D: It is contaminated with dangerous skin bacteria

explanation: That initial droplet usually mixes with clear tissue fluid from the skin poke, which throws off the glucose reading. Wiping it away gives you a true blood sample!

question: What is the primary focus of prevention in sexual health?

options.A: Eliminating all natural hormonal changes of aging
options.B: Curing long-term genetic disorders in adults
options.C: Stopping dysfunctions before they start or worsen
options.D: Prescribing hormone replacement therapy to everyone

explanation: Prevention aims to catch minor issues or stop risk factors early so they do not develop into chronic sexual dysfunctions. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h1)

question: How do transdermal patches differ from ordinary skin creams?

options.A: Transdermal patches are applied exclusively to mucous membranes
options.B: Patches only treat localized surface skin infections
options.C: Transdermal patches are designed for systemic absorption
options.D: Standard creams always enter the bloodstream faster than patches

explanation: While regular creams usually stay local, patches slowly deliver medicine through the skin and into the bloodstream to treat the entire body. Brilliant thinking!

question: How should a nurse respond when a patient expresses deep fear that their cancer will return?

options.A: Change the subject immediately to something more positive
options.B: Acknowledge their feelings and provide a safe space to talk
options.C: Assure them with certainty that the cancer will never come back
options.D: Tell them not to worry because worrying brings the cancer back

explanation: Empathy first! Validating their fears and being there to listen helps them process heavy emotions instead of bottling them up.

question: Why should you NEVER make a patient vomit after they swallow kerosene?

options.A: It makes the poison taste much worse on its way back up
options.B: It can cause the chemical to enter the lungs and cause aspiration pneumonia
options.C: It immediately neutralizes all medications given in the hospital
options.D: It causes instant blindness in both eyes

explanation: Well done! Coming back up, kerosene can easily slip into the windpipe and lungs, causing severe chemical pneumonia.

question: Which detail is most important for a home nurse to record during feeding visits?

options.A: Estimated percentage of meals eaten and weight trends
options.B: The exact brand of dishes used in the household
options.C: The grocery store prices of all purchased food
options.D: The names of visiting neighbors and friends

explanation: You got it! Tracking intake percentages and weight changes tells you clearly if the nutrition plan is working.

question: A head nurse wants to keep the ward staff motivated and aware of patient safety goals. Where is the run chart typically displayed for maximum team impact?

options.A: On a private website accessible only to hospital directors
options.B: Inside a locked filing cabinet in the manager's office
options.C: On a staff notice board in the clinical unit
options.D: In the patient's bedside personal medical chart

explanation: Displaying run charts openly in the unit keeps the frontline nursing team engaged and informed about quality metrics. [learn more](GST319_U1_T3#GST319_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which common virus is strongly linked to the development of cervical cancer?

options.A: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.B: Human Papillomavirus
options.C: Epstein-Barr virus
options.D: Hepatitis B virus

explanation: High-risk strains of HPV can cause changes in cervical cells over time. This is why screening and the HPV vaccine are such big wins in public health!

question: What structural feature keeps the trachea open and stops it from collapsing?

options.A: Smooth muscle sheets inside the lumen
options.B: Horseshoe-shaped cartilage rings
options.C: Dense networks of elastic ligaments
options.D: Thick layers of stratified epithelium

explanation: Think of those horseshoe-shaped cartilage rings as sturdy scaffolding that keeps the windpipe open against everyday neck pressures. Simple and brilliant!

question: What do we call infections that jump naturally between animals and humans?

options.A: Nosocomial infections
options.B: Autoimmune disorders
options.C: Zoonotic diseases
options.D: Chronic conditions

explanation: Zoonotic diseases are infections shared between animals and humans, like rabies or Lassa fever. Always good to keep this in mind for community health!

question: A patient has a chronic cough because their respiratory cilia are damaged. Which defence mechanism is directly affected?

options.A: Raising body temperature during a fever
options.B: Clearing trapped germs and mucus out of the airways
options.C: Swallowing bacteria with white blood cells
options.D: Producing antibodies against specific viruses

explanation: When cilia are damaged, they can't sweep out mucus and dirt, leaving the lungs wide open to infections. You've got this!

question: What does a patient's viral load test actually measure?

options.A: The exact percentage of body fat lost to lipodystrophy
options.B: The total number of remaining functional white blood cells
options.C: The total functional capacity of the patient's liver
options.D: The amount of active virus circulating in the blood

explanation: Viral load tells us how much of the virus is present in the bloodstream, showing how actively it is multiplying.

question: Why can transitioning from a hospital to home care be tough for a nurse?

options.A: Hospitals use entirely different medical terminology.
options.B: Hospitals do not teach any clinical procedures.
options.C: Home care requires autonomous decision-making without immediate medical backup.
options.D: Nurses in hospitals never interact with patients directly.

explanation: Correct! In the hospital, doctors and senior colleagues are close by. In home care, you often have to think and act independently.

question: Why is it important for a nurse to understand national economic factors?

options.A: Financial factors have no bearing on daily clinical nursing practice.
options.B: Nurses are solely responsible for setting national taxation rates.
options.C: Economic stress directly impacts a patient's ability to manage their health.
options.D: Understanding economics allows nurses to set hospital drug prices.

explanation: Poverty and financial instability influence whether a patient can afford medications, follow proper nutrition, or access care when needed. [learn more](GST322_U3_T7#GST322_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why is asking for healthcare different from buying regular everyday goods like shoes or food?

options.A: Patients can easily diagnose and prescribe their own meds
options.B: Healthcare services are always completely free from the government
options.C: Sickness usually happens without warning and patients need professional guidance
options.D: The supply of doctors and nurses is totally unlimited everywhere

explanation: Spot on! You can't really plan when you'll fall ill. Because medical needs come suddenly, patients rely heavily on expert advice rather than just shopping around casually.

question: A client wants a specific pill, but it is unsafe for her because she has severe high blood pressure. What should you do first?

options.A: Give her the requested pill anyway to make her happy
options.B: Send her straight to a big teaching hospital for surgery
options.C: Scold her for choosing a bad medication without asking
options.D: Explain the health risk gently and discuss safer options

explanation: You got it! Patient safety comes first. We calmly explain why a drug isn't safe and gladly help them pick a better alternative.

question: Why are gravies and sauces often added to meats on a soft diet?

options.A: To hide the taste of spoiled ingredients in the kitchen
options.B: To add moisture and prevent the meat from feeling dry during chewing
options.C: To change the color of the food to stimulate appetite
options.D: To dramatically increase the sodium content for hydration

explanation: Soft meats can easily become dry and difficult to swallow; gravies provide necessary lubrication. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h4)

question: Why do we say communication is a clinical intervention, just like giving medicine?

options.A: It requires a written doctor's prescription before it can occur.
options.B: It carries the exact same legal risks as giving an intravenous drug.
options.C: It directly influences patient health outcomes and healing environments.
options.D: It is recorded on the medication administration record every shift.

explanation: You got it! Just like a tablet or injection, the words you use can genuinely help a patient heal and feel better.

question: Which animal is the main carrier of the Lassa virus?

options.A: Domestic house cat
options.B: Mastomys rat
options.C: Ground squirrel
options.D: Fruit bat

explanation: The multimammate rat (Mastomys species) is the natural reservoir that carries and spreads the virus without getting sick itself.

question: According to the Hoehn and Yahr scale, what does Stage 1 Parkinson's disease mean?

options.A: Symptoms are limited to one side of the body with minimal disability.
options.B: Bilateral disease is present with severe impairment of balance.
options.C: Symptoms are completely absent during physical exertion.
options.D: The patient is confined strictly to a wheelchair or bed.

explanation: Stage 1 is the very beginning of the journey. The symptoms affect only one side of the body (unilateral) and cause very little disruption to daily life.

question: How do Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs) help fight HIV?

options.A: They dissolve the fatty outer envelope of the virus
options.B: They act as faulty building blocks to stop viral DNA creation
options.C: They physically block the outer cell membrane receptors
options.D: They destroy mature viral particles circulating in the plasma

explanation: Brilliant! NRTIs act like fake Lego pieces. When the virus tries to build its DNA, it grabs the fake piece and the process grinds to a halt.

question: How do day care services benefit family caregivers directly?

options.A: By offering financial loans for business start-ups
options.B: By reducing caregiver burnout through reliable respite
options.C: By permanently taking over full parental responsibilities
options.D: By providing free housing facilities for the whole family

explanation: Reliable daytime care gives parents and family caregivers time to work or rest, preventing severe physical and emotional exhaustion. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h2)

question: A patient arrives at the emergency unit completely unresponsive after a road accident. Where should you get their health history?

options.A: Family members, emergency personnel, and previous medical records
options.B: Waiting until the patient wakes up before gathering any information
options.C: Guessing the past medical history based on the patient's age
options.D: Asking the patient's coworkers who are standing outside the room

explanation: Great job! When a patient can't speak for themselves, family members and past medical files are lifesavers for gathering background info.

question: Which group is most likely covered by strict mandatory reporting laws that require action even without adult consent?

options.A: Adults with minor self-limiting acute illnesses
options.B: Older adults and individuals with severe disabilities
options.C: College students living in campus housing
options.D: Financially independent working adults

explanation: Spot on! Vulnerable groups like seniors and disabled individuals have special legal protections that mean nurses must report suspected abuse.

question: A patient suddenly collapses after being stung by a bee. What substance did the bee inject to cause this?

options.A: Insect venom
options.B: Bacterial toxin
options.C: Parasitic larvae
options.D: Fungal spores

explanation: Insect stings deliver venom packed with proteins that can act as powerful allergens in sensitive people.

question: What triggers the baby's circulatory system to close its fetal blood shunts?

options.A: Putting eye ointment in
options.B: Changes in oxygen levels and clamping the cord
options.C: The vernix washing away
options.D: Brown fat kicking in

explanation: When the cord is clamped and the baby takes that first big breath, oxygen levels change in the chest, telling those temporary fetal shunts to close up.

question: A patient contracts a skin infection after touching a blood pressure cuff that was used on a previous infected patient without being cleaned. What type of transmission is this?

options.A: Common vehicle water transmission
options.B: Vector-borne transmission
options.C: Airborne droplet nuclei transmission
options.D: Indirect contact transmission

explanation: Because the germ traveled from the first patient to the cuff and then to the second patient, it is indirect contact through a fomite. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h3)

question: A patient with an undetectable viral load for over a year asks if they can still pass the virus sexually. What is the best response?

options.A: Transmission can only happen if they stop eating fresh fruits
options.B: They can only transmit the virus during the rainy season
options.C: Transmission is still just as likely as before starting treatment
options.D: The risk of sexual transmission is effectively zero as long as adherence is maintained

explanation: Brilliant! This is what we call U=U (Undetectable equals Untransmittable). When a patient takes their meds and stays undetectable, they cannot pass the virus sexually.

question: How is cholera primarily passed to humans?

options.A: Through direct skin-to-skin contact
options.B: Through contaminated water and food
options.C: By inhaling airborne respiratory droplets
options.D: Via the bite of infected mosquitoes

explanation: Swallowing water or food polluted with tiny traces of waste is how the bacteria enters our digestive system. Good hygiene stops it!

question: What is the main purpose of wearing Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)?

options.A: To create a physical barrier between the nurse and infectious hazards
options.B: To hide the nurse's facial expressions from anxious family members
options.C: To comply with fashion trends established by hospital management
options.D: To keep the nurse's personal clothing clean from everyday dust

explanation: PPE acts like your personal shield, stopping germs, chemicals, and fluids from touching your skin or clothes.

question: How does severe income inequality affect the overall health of a population?

options.A: It eliminates chronic stress among lower-income earners.
options.B: It completely stops the spread of infectious diseases.
options.C: It places a heavy disease burden on poorer groups who cannot afford early care.
options.D: It ensures that everyone has equal access to private clinics.

explanation: Wide gaps in wealth mean poorer citizens cannot afford preventive care or early treatment, allowing minor sicknesses to develop into severe, chronic illnesses. [learn more](GST322_U3_T7#GST322_U3_T7_h2)

question: Which specific mineral ion is mainly responsible for making things taste salty?

options.A: Potassium
options.B: Hydrogen
options.C: Sodium
options.D: Calcium

explanation: Sodium ions rush right into special channels on the cell, firing up the membrane to send a 'salt' signal to your brain.

question: What does the systolic blood pressure reading measure?

options.A: The pressure when the heart rests
options.B: The total volume of blood in the body
options.C: The pressure when the heart beats
options.D: The speed of blood flow in veins

explanation: Systolic pressure represents the force in the arteries when the heart muscle contracts to pump blood forward. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T14#GNS214_U1_T14_h1)

question: What does Gross National Product (GNP) measure?

options.A: The total value of goods and services produced by a country's citizens
options.B: The total cost of running public hospitals across the country
options.C: The total expenditure on imported drugs and medical equipment
options.D: The total amount of money borrowed by the federal government annually

explanation: Think of GNP as the big picture: it adds up the total value of everything produced by a nation's citizens and businesses, no matter where in the world they are working. You've got this!

question: What do we mean by 'microbial load' in a hospital or clinic?

options.A: The total number of microorganisms on a contaminated object
options.B: The specific type of chemical disinfectant used on instruments
options.C: The weight of dry garbage collected in a hospital ward
options.D: The maximum capacity limit of an incinerator furnace

explanation: You've got this! Microbial load simply refers to the total count of living germs on a surface or waste item. The higher the load, the more dangerous that item is if someone handles it carelessly.

question: What do we call computer hardware?

options.A: The invisible programs and operating instructions
options.B: The secret password protection protocols for patient files
options.C: The physical, touchable parts of the computer system
options.D: The wireless network signals inside a hospital ward

explanation: Think of hardware as anything you can physically touch, like the monitor, keyboard, or mouse at the nursing station.

question: What is one of the biggest barriers stopping adolescents from seeking STI testing and treatment?

options.A: Too many hours spent in school classes
options.B: Excessive availability of free condoms
options.C: Overabundance of trained nurses in clinics
options.D: Fear of social stigma and judgment

explanation: Correct! Fear of being judged or gossiped about often makes teenagers keep quiet and delay getting the medical help they need.

question: Why might a doctor perform a therapeutic lumbar puncture?

options.A: To remove a kidney stone from the ureter
options.B: To check the patient's blood glucose level
options.C: To lower high pressure inside the skull
options.D: To clear an airway blockage in the lungs

explanation: You got it! Removing extra fluid during the procedure helps relieve dangerous pressure inside the skull when there is a fluid buildup.

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical socioeconomic benefit of family planning for a household?

options.A: Increased ability to afford nutritious food and clothing
options.B: Higher likelihood of children completing their education
options.C: Reduced spending on emergency medical care for sick infants
options.D: Guaranteed employment for all children upon reaching adulthood

explanation: Family planning improves financial management and education access, but it does not automatically guarantee employment for children later in life. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h3)

question: Why is it important to check the discussion section for study limitations?

options.A: It replaces the need to read the results section
options.B: It shows whether the authors are honest about what their study could not prove
options.C: It tells the reader how much money the research project cost
options.D: It provides a list of spelling corrections for the final publication

explanation: Acknowledging limitations helps readers understand where the study might be weak or where results cannot be generalized. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h3)

question: How many sections make up the abdominopelvic quadrant system?
explanation: The abdominopelvic area is split into four quadrants for rapid clinical screening during assessments. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h4)

question: When should a nurse separate contaminated materials from regular waste?

options.A: At the point of generation
options.B: Only when an infection is confirmed
options.C: After the waste reaches the incinerator
options.D: During the end-of-shift cleanup

explanation: Waste must be sorted right where it is used to prevent accidental exposure during later handling. [learn more](GST114_U2_T14#GST114_U2_T14_h1)

question: How does carrying excess body weight contribute directly to knee osteoarthritis?

options.A: It increases mechanical stress on weight-bearing joints and promotes inflammation
options.B: It stops the body from producing normal synovial fluid
options.C: It causes the leg muscles to weaken and shrink away completely
options.D: It blocks calcium from reaching the bone ends inside the joint

explanation: Extra weight forces the knee joints to bear heavier loads with every step, and fat tissue also releases chemicals that trigger joint inflammation. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h2)

question: A patient with completely clear breathing sounds inhaled a toxic gas two hours ago. What should you, as the nurse, expect to do?

options.A: Withholding all intravenous fluids to prevent lung fluid overload
options.B: Ordering a baseline chest X-ray and monitoring for delayed edema
options.C: Performing an immediate surgical tracheostomy in the ward
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately since lungs are currently clear

explanation: Don't let clear lungs fool you! Inhaled toxins can trigger dangerous fluid buildup (edema) in the lungs hours later, so keep a close eye on them.

question: Where does the heart medication digoxin originally come from?

options.A: Bovine pancreas tissue
options.B: Foxglove plant
options.C: Magnesium rock beds
options.D: Synthetic petroleum

explanation: Fun fact! Digoxin is a classic heart medicine originally extracted from the purple foxglove plant.

question: What is the main difference between anabolism and catabolism?

options.A: Anabolism produces waste products, while catabolism produces vitamins
options.B: Anabolism occurs in the stomach, while catabolism happens in the liver
options.C: Anabolism deals only with fats, while catabolism processes water
options.D: Anabolism builds up body tissues, while catabolism breaks down molecules for energy

explanation: Well remembered! Think of anabolism as building up (like construction) and catabolism as breaking down (like demolition to release energy).

question: Why do water quality testers measure turbidity?

options.A: To calculate the total mineral salt content in wells
options.B: To measure the exact temperature of the water source
options.C: To determine the amount of dissolved oxygen available
options.D: To check how cloudy the water is from suspended particles

explanation: Great job! Turbidity just means cloudiness. High cloudiness is dangerous because it hides harmful germs from water treatment chemicals.

question: How do free radicals and reactive oxygen species primarily damage our cells?

options.A: By stimulating excessive and uncontrollable cellular reproduction
options.B: By instantly freezing intracellular fluid and stopping circulation
options.C: By creating oxidative stress that harms DNA and cell membranes
options.D: By completely blocking the intake of dietary proteins

explanation: Free radicals love to steal electrons from nearby molecules. This creates oxidative stress, which can rough up essential parts of the cell like our DNA and protective membranes.

question: Which of these is a typical source of chemical waste in a hospital?

options.A: Leftover food trays from patient bedsides
options.B: Paper wrappers from sterile surgical gloves
options.C: Discarded lab reagents and cleaning solvents
options.D: Cotton wool balls soaked in sterile water

explanation: You'll find chemical waste coming from cleaning supplies, disinfectants, and laboratory testing chemicals.

question: What is the primary purpose of a health care budget?

options.A: To eliminate all unexpected hospital expenses permanently
options.B: To calculate exact salaries for individual doctors and nurses
options.C: To plan and control financial resources for medical services
options.D: To set the retail prices of medications in the pharmacy

explanation: A health care budget serves as a financial plan to guide how money is spent on patient care services. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h1)

question: A flexible scope touches a patient's mucous membranes during a test. According to the Spaulding rule, how should this item be processed?

options.A: Standard low-level wiping
options.B: Terminal steam sterilization
options.C: Simple soap and water washing
options.D: High-level disinfection

explanation: Items touching mucous membranes are semi-critical! While they don't always need full autoclaving, they definitely need high-level disinfection to knock out stubborn germs and viruses.

question: Why is building trust so important during a reproductive health check-in?

options.A: It prevents the patient from asking questions about treatment costs
options.B: It encourages the patient to share sensitive personal information honestly
options.C: It guarantees the patient will accept all prescribed medications
options.D: It replaces the need for a detailed physical examination

explanation: Great nursing care starts with a good relationship! When patients trust you, they feel safe sharing personal details about their sexual or menstrual health without fear of judgment.

question: What is the difference between disease elimination and disease eradication?

options.A: Elimination is a global status, while eradication is restricted to local clinics.
options.B: Eradication only applies to non-communicable lifestyle disorders.
options.C: Elimination requires no further interventions, while eradication requires constant vaccination.
options.D: Eradication means worldwide disappearance, while elimination means zero cases in a specific region.

explanation: Spot on! Elimination stops local spread in a specific country or zone, but eradication wipes out the pathogen globally forever.

question: Which of the following is a core clinical duty included in community midwifery practice?

options.A: Conducting routine physical checks and monitoring antenatal clients
options.B: Diagnosing and treating chronic adult medical diseases
options.C: Performing major surgical procedures like cesarean sections
options.D: Prescribing permanent contraceptive surgeries for adolescents

explanation: Antenatal monitoring, managing normal deliveries, and postnatal checks fall squarely within the standard scope of practice for a community midwife. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h2)

question: During which step of mobilisation do community members and nurses figure out what resources and tasks are needed?

options.A: Immediate closure
options.B: Final evaluation
options.C: Strict policing
options.D: Action planning

explanation: Action planning is where the community maps out tasks, responsibilities, and timelines using local resources. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h5)

question: What important health protection do hormonal contraceptives fail to provide that you must always emphasize to clients?

options.A: Protection against sexually transmitted infections
options.B: Prevention of severe uterine cramping pain
options.C: Protection against common bacterial skin rashes
options.D: Prevention of irregular monthly spotting

explanation: Never forget: birth control pills prevent pregnancy, but they do NOT stop STIs. Always remind clients to pair them with barrier methods like condoms!

question: During a massive flood, what is the primary role of security agencies like the police?

options.A: Crowd control, maintenance of law and order, and safe corridors
options.B: Designing permanent structural housing for displaced families
options.C: Clinical triage and emergency surgical interventions at the bedside
options.D: Purchasing medical equipment and pharmaceutical drugs from abroad

explanation: Police and civil defense keep people safe, manage crowds, and clear paths so medical teams can get through.

question: Why is finding protein persistently in a patient's urine an important warning sign?

options.A: It confirms that the liver is failing to process dietary nutrients properly.
options.B: It shows that the bladder is contracting too frequently during the day.
options.C: It indicates that the filtering barriers of the glomeruli have been damaged.
options.D: It proves that the patient is eating too much protein in their daily diet.

explanation: Healthy glomeruli act like a strict bouncer, keeping big protein molecules safely inside the blood. If protein leaks into the urine, it tells us those filters are injured.

question: Why do cancer cells keep growing even after the original tissue injury is gone?

options.A: They receive constant growth signals from nearby nerves
options.B: Scar tissue forces them to keep dividing rapidly
options.C: The body actively pumps extra blood into the tumor
options.D: Their internal regulatory machinery is permanently damaged

explanation: You got this! Inside these cells, the internal control buttons are broken, so they keep multiplying on their own without needing an outside trigger.
